$comment: Leg and controller catalog. Single source of truth for identifiers used by the service request forms, the parts reference, and the firmware manifest. A leg is the durable asset; there is no persistent machine above it.

legVariants.name: Standard Leg
legVariants.notes: Baseline leg. Stands unsupported on its three-caster tripod. Shares no wiring, bus, or rigidity with any other leg.

legVariants.name: Standard Leg, High-Stroke
legVariants.notes: Extended lift travel for tall station variants. Interchangeable with LEG-S in any module pairing.

legVariants.name: Early Leg (Pilot)
legVariants.notes: Pilot-fleet leg. BRK-U1 does not fit current rail without KIT-U1U2. CC-0 accepts no remote firmware; updates are applied at ERS by cable.

controllers.name: ClearCore (Pilot Build)
controllers.notes: No signed-update support. Reflashed by cable during an ERS visit.

controllers.name: ClearCore (Production)
controllers.notes: Accepts signed bundles relayed from a session controller over XBee. The leg itself has no internet path.

sessionControllers.name: Session Controller
sessionControllers.notes: Pairs legs into modules, holds the session, and is the only device on the network that reaches this portal. Firmware for legs arrives here first, then fans out over XBee.

moduleRange.description: A module is a left plus right leg paired in software only. Longer stations claim more modules. Pairing is arbitrary and is re-formed every session.

electronics.label: Electronics serial
electronics.description: The leg's operational identity: the number its ClearCore reports, shown by the ERS tablet when the controller is connected and on the session controller roster. Swapping the electronics rolls this over — firmware and pairing follow it.

mechanical.label: Mechanical serial
mechanical.description: Stamped on the leg frame as (side)-(version)(product initial)(manufacture order number), for example L-V3BE123. Permanent for the life of the leg. Motor-hours and gearbox wear accrue against this number, not the electronics.
